title: Molecular Mechanism of Epimedium Extract against Ischemic Stroke Based on Network Pharmacology and Experimental Validation.
authors: Xu, Hongbei; You, Mingyao; Xiang, Xiang; Zhao, Jun; Yuan, Ping; Chu, Lan; Xie, Chenchen
one_liner_zh: 该文基于网络药理学和实验验证研究淫羊藿抗缺血性卒中的分子机制，核心是药物-疾病靶点通路，无蛋白质-DNA互作体系、无结合建模，亦无AI或物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Ischemic stroke exhibits high morbidity, disability, and mortality, and treatments for ischemic stroke are limited despite intensive research. The potent neuroprotective benefits of Epimedium against ischemic stroke have gained lots of interest. Nevertheless, systematic research on the direct role and mechanisms of Epimedium in ischemic stroke is still lacking. Network pharmacology analysis coupled with experimental verification was utilized to systematically evaluate the potential pharmacological mechanism of Epimedium against ischemic stroke. The TCMSP database was used to mine the bioactive ingredients and Epimedium's targets. The DrugBank, OMIM, and GeneCards databases were employed to identify potential targets of ischemic stroke. GO and KEGG pathway analyses were also carried out. The interaction between active components and hub targets was confirmed via molecular docking. An experimental ischemic stroke model was used to evaluate the possible therapeutic mechanism of Epimedium. As a result, 23 bioactive compounds of Epimedium were selected, and 30 hub targets of Epimedium in its function against ischemic stroke were identified, and molecular docking results demonstrated good binding. The IL-17 signaling pathway was revealed as a potentially significant pathway, with the NF-kappaB and MAPK/ERK signaling pathways being involved. Furthermore, in vivo experiments demonstrated that Epimedium treatment could improve neurological function and reduce infarct volume. Additionally, Epimedium reduced the activation of microglia and astrocytes in both the ischemic penumbra of the hippocampus and cerebral cortex following ischemic stroke. Western blot and RT-qPCR analyses demonstrated that Epimedium not only depressed the expression of IL-1beta, TNF-alpha, IL-6, and IL-4 but also inhibited the NF-kappaB and MAPK/ERK signaling pathways. This study applied network pharmacology and in vivo experiment to explore possible mechanism of Epimedium's role against ischemic stroke, which provides insight into the treatment of ischemic stroke.
abstract_zh: 缺血性卒中具有高发病率、高致残率和高死亡率，尽管进行了大量研究，但其治疗方法仍然有限。淫羊藿对缺血性卒中的强效神经保护作用引起了广泛关注。然而，关于淫羊藿在缺血性卒中中直接作用及机制的系统性研究仍缺乏。本研究采用网络药理学分析结合实验验证，系统评估淫羊藿抗缺血性卒中的潜在药理机制。利用TCMSP数据库挖掘淫羊藿的生物活性成分及其靶点。通过DrugBank、OMIM和GeneCards数据库识别缺血性卒中的潜在靶点。同时进行了GO和KEGG通路分析。通过分子对接确认活性成分与核心靶点之间的相互作用。采用实验性缺血性卒中模型评估淫羊藿可能的治疗机制。结果显示，筛选出淫羊藿的23种生物活性化合物，并确定了淫羊藿在抗缺血性卒中作用中的30个核心靶点，分子对接结果显示出良好的结合能力。IL-17信号通路被揭示为潜在的重要通路，其中涉及NF-kappaB和MAPK/ERK信号通路。此外，体内实验表明，淫羊藿治疗可改善神经功能并减少梗死体积。另外，淫羊藿在缺血性卒中后减少了海马和大脑皮层缺血半暗带中小胶质细胞和星形胶质细胞的激活。Western blot和RT-qPCR分析表明，淫羊藿不仅抑制了IL-1beta、TNF-alpha、IL-6和IL-4的表达，还抑制了NF-kappaB和MAPK/ERK信号通路。本研究应用网络药理学和体内实验探索了淫羊藿抗缺血性卒中的可能机制，为缺血性卒中的治疗提供了见解。
